subsystems.name: Storage cavity
subsystems.role: holds the quantum state as a superposition of two coherent microwave states of opposite phase.
parts: superconducting λ/2 or lumped-element microwave resonator

subsystems.name: Nonlinear stabilising element
subsystems.role: supplies the two-photon drive and two-photon dissipation that pump the two coherent states apart and keep them apart.
parts: Josephson junctions (often in a SNAIL or similar loop)
pump line at twice the cavity frequency

subsystems.name: Ancilla and readout
subsystems.role: a separate superconducting qubit that measures the cavity's parity without destroying the encoded state.
parts: dispersive coupling to the storage cavity

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and microwave infrastructure
subsystems.role: keeps the chip cold and delivers clean, filtered signals.

subsystems.name: Bias-preserving logic
subsystems.role: gates that manipulate logical states without converting the rare bit flips into common phase flips.

subsystems.name: Classical decoding
subsystems.role: reads the parity syndromes and tracks the phase errors they reveal.

buildSteps.title: Design the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Choose the cavity frequency, the strength of the nonlinear element and the two-photon drive amplitude. Larger coherent-state separation means exponentially rarer bit flips, but a more demanding resonator.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the chip
buildSteps.detail: Deposit a niobium film on a sapphire or silicon wafer and pattern the resonators with lithography; build aluminium–aluminium oxide–aluminium Josephson junctions by shadow evaporation in a single vacuum step.

buildSteps.title: Cool the package
buildSteps.detail: Mount the chip in a dilution refrigerator and cool it to around 10 millikelvin, below the superconducting transition and low enough to empty the microwave modes of thermal photons.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the bare hardware
buildSteps.detail: Measure cavity resonance, photon lifetime and the ancilla qubit's frequency and dispersive coupling, then calibrate the pump line.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise a cat state
buildSteps.detail: Drive the nonlinear element at twice the cavity frequency so the two-photon processes create and maintain the two-lobed state; tomograph its Wigner function to confirm the lobes.

buildSteps.title: Measure the error bias
buildSteps.detail: Run the state over time and count bit flips versus phase flips to verify that bit flips are suppressed exponentially with the size of the coherent states.

buildSteps.title: Add error-correcting logic
buildSteps.detail: Chain several cat qubits and repeatedly measure parity to detect phase flips, while gates are tuned to be bias-preserving.

buildSteps.title: Scale the processor
buildSteps.detail: Wire many cavities together, route pumps and readout lines, and move control electronics into the fridge or into cryogenic integrated circuits to keep the wiring manageable.

prerequisites.why: the cavity, ancilla and nonlinear element all come from standard Josephson-junction processes.
stabilising coherent-state superpositions by driving a nonlinear cavity was demonstrated in the mid-2010s, but with modest lifetimes and few devices.
bit-flip protection grows with the number of photons the cavity can hold before one leaks away.
repetition codes tailored to a one-sided error channel were worked out in the 2010s.
most two-qubit gates leak phase errors into bit errors, which would erase the hardware advantage.
the ancilla's own errors set a floor on how well parity can be measured.

pathway.milestone: single cat qubits in dilution refrigerators with bit-flip lifetimes far longer than their phase-flip lifetimes, and small parity-measurement demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the bias is real and tunable in hardware.

pathway.milestone: a few-qubit repetition code that corrects phase flips and shows a logical lifetime longer than its best physical component
pathway.unlocks: first proof that the biased-error architecture saves hardware.

pathway.milestone: bias-preserving entangling gates and a second, outer code layer for the residual bit flips
pathway.unlocks: a fully protected logical qubit built from far fewer physical elements than an unbiased design would need.

pathway.milestone: arrays of logical qubits with integrated cryogenic control
pathway.unlocks: a route to fault-tolerant machines small enough to build and cool.
